lines.text: A narrow strip of land between two oceans, crossed by conquistadors, gold, pirates and finally a canal. This is the story of Panama.
In 1513 Vasco Nunez de Balboa crossed the isthmus and became the first European to see the Pacific from the Americas.
In 1519 the Spanish founded Panama on the Pacific shore. Silver and gold from Peru passed through, until the pirate Henry Morgan sacked it.
Two years after the sack, the city was rebuilt on a new site. It is today's Panama City.
By then Panama was part of Colombia. At the turn of the century a bloody civil war, the Thousand Days' War, tore Colombia apart.
In November 1903, after centuries under Spain and then Colombia, Panama became a country of its own.
Its break from Colombia was backed by the United States, which wanted to build a canal.
The French had failed. In 1914 the Americans opened the canal, with locks that lift ships over the hills, at a heavy cost in lives.
Omar Torrijos, a military leader, would win the treaties that gave the canal back to Panama.
Manuel Noriega would rule the country as a strongman, until the United States removed him.
Ruben Blades would become a salsa star, a film actor and a politician.
Jose Raul Mulino, born in 1959, would become president in 2024.
Mariano Rivera would become a great baseball pitcher, the first voted into the Hall of Fame by every single voter.
In 1977 Torrijos and President Carter signed the treaties: the canal would pass to Panama at the end of the century.
In December 1989 American troops invaded Panama and ousted Noriega.
Panama took the canal over in 1999, and in 2016 opened new, larger locks for the world's giant ships.
That same year millions of leaked files from a Panama law firm showed how the powerful hid money offshore.
Where two oceans almost meet, Panama now holds the key between them.
